docRequirement: workflows.md:227 binds the `args` global to the invocation value verbatim: "Claude passes the list as structured data, so the script can call array and object methods on `args` directly without parsing it first. If `args` is omitted, the global is `undefined` inside the script." So a saved or plugin workflow run with no input must see `args === undefined`, which is what makes the `args ?? default`, `if (!args)` and `args === undefined` idioms in a script work.
current: The workflow runtime coalesces an omitted `args` to an empty object at BOTH invocation chokepoints. Top-level run: `returnValue = await compiledScript(makeApi(input.args ?? {}));` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/workflow-tool.ts:750). Nested in-script helper: `return await compileWorkflowScript(source)(makeApi(recipeArgs ?? {}));` (workflow-tool.ts:660). Nothing else defaults it — `normalizeInput` carries the value through unchanged (`args: params.args`, workflow-tool.ts:186), the tool schema marks it optional ('Optional JSON value exposed inside the script as args.', workflow-tool.ts:436), `makeApi` assigns it straight onto the api (`args: runtimeArgs`, workflow-tool.ts:728), and the sandbox injects `api.args` verbatim as the `args` Function parameter (packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/sandbox.ts:285, :297, :345). Measured on this HEAD by compiling `return JSON.stringify({typeofArgs: typeof args, isUndefined: args === undefined, falsy: !args, nullishDefault: (args ?? 'DEFAULT-BRANCH')})` through the real `compileWorkflowScript`: with our call-site expression (`undefined ?? {}`) → {"typeofArgs":"object","isUndefined":false,"falsy":false,"nullishDefault":{}}; positive control, the same script with the value passed through unmodified → {"typeofArgs":"undefined","isUndefined":true,"falsy":true,"nullishDefault":"DEFAULT-BRANCH"}. A second, independent chokepoint sits one layer up on the user-facing path: the slash-command RPC always attaches args, even when the user typed no tail — `const args = message.trim()` then `workflowInvocation = { ...command.workflowInvocation, args: { input: args } }` (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:322, :337-340), so `/my-workflow` with no trailing text reaches the tool as `args = { input: '' }`. The command records themselves carry no args (`workflowInvocation: { name: recipe.meta.name }` for saved workflows, packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:15881; `workflowInvocation: { script: parsed.source }` for plugin workflows, SessionManager.ts:16158), so the RPC layer is the sole producer. Both paths funnel into workflow-tool.ts:750, and saved (`name`) and plugin (`scriptPath`/`script`) sources resolve into the same run (workflow-tool.ts:236-243, :750).
divergence: The value is wrong, not the key: `args` is spelled correctly and reaches the script correctly whenever it is supplied — the only delta is the substitution performed when it is NOT supplied. Claude leaves the global `undefined`; we hand the script `{}` (workflow-tool.ts:750 and :660), and on the slash path we hand it `{ input: '' }` (sessions.ts:337-340). Consequence: every documented no-input branch (`args === undefined`, `!args`, `args ?? default`) is unreachable, because `{}` is both defined and truthy. In the opposite direction our behaviour is more lenient than the spec — `args.foo` yields `undefined` here where Claude throws a TypeError — so no script errors out; it silently takes the wrong branch.

change.what: One line. `returnValue = await compiledScript(makeApi(input.args ?? {}));` becomes `returnValue = await compiledScript(makeApi(input.args));`. `makeApi(runtimeArgs: unknown)` and `WorkflowRuntimeApi.args: unknown` already accept undefined, so no type change. Add a short comment citing workflows.md:227 so the coalescing is not reintroduced.

One line, same edit: `compileWorkflowScript(source)(makeApi(recipeArgs ?? {}))` becomes `compileWorkflowScript(source)(makeApi(recipeArgs))`. Without it a nested `workflow('other')` call still injects `{}` and the divergence survives one level down.

change.symbol: it('contains a hostile synchronous script instead of blocking the subprocess'), lines 48-50
change.what: MUST change or the fix turns this test red. The script is `'const start = args; while (start !== undefined) { }'` and it relies on the current `{}` substitution to spin; with `args` undefined the loop body never executes and the expected 'synchronous execution' error never fires. Keep the intent by passing args explicitly in the execute call: `tool.execute('call', { script: 'const start = args; while (start !== undefined) { }', args: {} }, ...)`.

change.symbol: new test, e.g. it('leaves the args global undefined when the invocation omits args')
change.what: Two cases against the real tool: (a) execute with `{ script: "return typeof args;" }` and no `args` key → `details.returnValue === 'undefined'`; (b) execute with `{ script: "return args ?? 'DEFAULT';" , args: { input: 'x' } }` → the supplied object comes back unchanged. Optionally a third for the nested helper: a recipe whose source is `return typeof args;` invoked as `workflow('key')` with no second argument.

Separable but it is what makes the fix reach a user. `workflowInvocation = { ...command.workflowInvocation, args: { input: args } }` becomes `workflowInvocation = { ...command.workflowInvocation, ...(args ? { args: { input: args } } : {}) }` so a tail-less `/my-workflow` leaves `args` absent on the wire and therefore `undefined` in the script. `args` here is already `message.trim()` (line 322), so the empty-tail case is exactly `args === ''`. The existing RPC test (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/__tests__/sessions-custom-slash-command.test.ts:98-107) passes a non-empty tail and stays green; add a sibling case asserting the invocation has no `args` key when the tail is empty.

blastRadius: Same-package callers: `handleWorkflowExecute` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:3711-3740) hands `msg.invocation` straight to `activeWorkflowCommandTool.execute`, and the tool is otherwise reached by the model calling `workflow` directly. Wire boundary — flag as a risk trigger even though no schema changes: `WorkflowInvocation` (packages/shared/src/agent/backend/types.ts:691-696, `args?: unknown`) travels host → Pi subprocess as `WorkflowExecuteMessage.invocation` (packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:265-277) via `requestWorkflowExecution` (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6260-6286). JSON cannot carry `undefined`, so an omitted key already arrives omitted and `normalizeInput` (workflow-tool.ts:186) leaves it undefined — the fix needs no envelope change, but it does change what a subprocess script observes across that boundary. Tests that touch this: workflow-tool.test.ts:48-50 (breaks, see change list), workflow-tool.test.ts:111-130 (passes args explicitly, unaffected), sandbox.test.ts:16/72/89/199 (all pass `args` explicitly, unaffected), workflow-real-server.test.ts:326 and :428-429 and packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-slash-workflow-turn.test.ts:118 (fixtures that construct `args: { input: '' }` themselves — unaffected by the tool fix; only the sessions.ts edit changes what production builds). Persistence: none — `args` is per-invocation and is not written to the journal or the recipe files. Imported-plugin path: Claude plugin `workflows/` scripts are imported verbatim (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:157, :314, :2606) and dispatch through SessionManager.ts:16158 into the same runtime, so the behaviour change applies to third-party Claude-authored scripts too. Behaviour-change risk worth naming: a script already written against today's `{}` that does `args.input` unconditionally will start throwing `Cannot read properties of undefined` instead of silently reading undefined — that is the documented Claude behaviour, but it is a change for scripts saved before the fix.
userImpact: Today, running a saved or plugin workflow with no input never takes its no-input path. Concretely: the user types `/release-audit` in the composer with no trailing text; the RPC layer sends `args: { input: '' }` (sessions.ts:337-340) and, on the tool-call route, the runtime substitutes `{}` (workflow-tool.ts:750). A script written to Claude's documented idiom — `const target = args ?? 'HEAD'`, or `if (!args) { return usage() }`, or `const files = args === undefined ? await discover() : args.files` — silently takes the has-input branch and runs against `{}`/`''`: agents get prompts with a blank target, a fan-out over an empty list produces zero or one empty item, and the run reports success. No error surfaces anywhere, so the user sees a workflow that 'ran' and did nothing useful, with nothing in the transcript naming the cause. This is not hypothetical for imported content — Claude plugin workflows are loaded verbatim and are exactly the scripts written to that page's idiom. For workflows our own model authors it is latent, because the prompt guidance tells it to read `args.input` (workflow-tool.ts:410, :413) rather than to branch on absence.
notes: Every cited line was read on this HEAD (workflow-tool.ts via Read of ranges 160-270, 400-470, 600-800; sandbox.ts verbatim via codegraph; sessions.ts 310-380; SessionManager.ts 15855-15900 and 16140-16170; custom-commands.ts 250-273; backend/types.ts 691-696; pi-agent.ts 6260-6286; index.ts 255-277 and 3700-3770; the tests as quoted). The `{}` consequence was re-measured independently of the challenger with the positive control described in `current`. Two things I did NOT verify and that are out of this finding's scope: (1) whether wrapping the raw tail as `{ input: <string> }` matches Claude's 'passes the list as structured data' shaping at all — our slash path never produces a structured value, only a string in a fixed envelope, which is a separate divergence on the same page; (2) how `$ARGUMENTS` in `workflowSlashCommandBody` (packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:271-273) interacts with the deterministic invocation when both are present — the body is substituted into `modelMessage` at sessions.ts:334 while the structured invocation wins the dispatch, and I did not trace which one the model ultimately sees.
